title: Train on your own output. What's lost?
hook: Each model learns from the last one's words. Can a rare word survive?

knows: that models learn word frequencies from data
that a model's output can end up in the next model's training data
doesNotKnow: that retraining on a model's own samples loses rare things permanently

misconception: Averaging over many samples preserves the distribution.
objective: The learner can explain that each generation trained on samples of the last can only lose rare items, never regain them, so a loop of models trained on model output narrows.

claims.text: A word that is 2% of the data is missed by all 50 draws with chance 0.98^50 = 36.4%; once its count is 0 it can never be drawn again.
claims.source: Independent draws: (1 − 0.02)^50 = 0.3642. Absorption at 0 follows from drawing only from current frequencies (nextGen in Demo.tsx). exactLoss(50) in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: In 2,000 seeded runs, the 2% word vanished after one generation 37.3% of the time.
claims.source: lossRate(50, 2000) in Demo.tsx, runs 1-2000 (seed run*1000 + generation into mulberry32), untuned. The stage shows runs 1, 2, 3, ... in order, also untuned: run 1 has lost 5 of 10 words by generation 3, and runs 1-10 each lost 4-6 words by generation 11.

claims.text: With 500 draws per generation the 2% word is lost in one generation with chance 0.98^500 ≈ 0.004%, but losses still only accumulate.
claims.source: exactLoss(500) = 4.1e-5 in Demo.tsx; lossRate(500, 2000) = 0 in 2,000 seeded runs.

claims.text: The toy resamples word counts only; it has no real model, and the ten words are invented.
claims.source: Brief 30 in company/domains/briefs/ai.md; labelled on the stage and in the reveal.

claims.text: Real models trained recursively on model-generated data lose the rare cases (the tails of the distribution) first.
claims.source: About real systems: Shumailov et al. 2024, 'AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data', Nature 631, 755-759.

recall.question: A photo generator is retrained each year mostly on photos made by last year's version. What should you expect to happen to unusual subjects?
options: They become rarer and some disappear for good
They stay as common as they were, on average
They become more common, because models like variety
recall.why: Each round samples from the last round's output, so a rare subject can miss a round by chance, and once missing it cannot come back. The losses pile up.
